result:
The api died because the disk filled up: the `report-export` job wrote about 20 GB of CSVs to `/var/lib/stockroom` in eight minutes, the database ran out of space, and the api exited and never came back.

One thing to check: the log's timestamps are all 2026-03-09 (02:00–05:30), not last night, so confirm this is the file you meant.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 03:05:00 | `report-export` starts writing 512 MB files to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, one every 12 seconds |
| 03:09:03 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 91%` |
| 03:12:48 | Last export file written (40 files in total) |
| 03:13:30 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 99%` |
| 03:14:00 | `ERROR db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device` |
| 03:14:03 | `ERROR api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool` |
| 03:14:06 | `FATAL api: exiting (status 1)` |
| 03:16:00 onwards | `ERROR proxy: upstream api refused connection` every 2 minutes, 67 times, the last at 05:28:00 |

- **Not recovered in this log:** there are no api requests or restart messages after 03:14:06, and the proxy was still being refused when the log ends at 05:29:57. The api was down for at least 2 h 15 min.
- **Other services:** `web` and `proxy` kept returning 200s for their own requests throughout.
- **Cache warnings are unrelated:** the `cache: slow command` warnings (100–150 ms) appear every ~5 minutes from the first line of the log, well before the incident, and don't change around it.
- **Export job:** the log shows no completion or failure message for it, so I can't tell whether it finished or was cut off by the full disk.

The exports and the database share the `/var/lib/stockroom` volume, which is why a batch job could take the api down. Nothing in the repo outside the log references `report-export`, so I couldn't see how it is scheduled or why it wrote so much.

Before restarting the api, space needs to be freed in `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, or it will fail the same way.
